title: The same account three months on: the purchase-order number asked for first
purpose: Story S1. The same fleet manager, another van. Before she pulls the van up Maya asks for the purchase-order number and reads it back; she offers a time, books it on the number and sums up the time, the work and the number.

mentioned.name: Donna Ledford
mentioned.role: the bookkeeper who sends the account's statements

call.day: the Wednesday of week T-4 (rule R6; card S01, call 24)

scenario.who_calls: Lonnie Coffey, fleet manager of company account A1.
scenario.vehicle: unit ND-08, a 2021 Ford Transit-250, BRC-6125 (accounts.json en.A1 fleet)
scenario.job: fleet PM service A, due; and a steering-wheel shake at 60 mph to check
scenario.what_happens: Maya asks for the purchase-order number first and reads it back, finds the unit by its tag, asks at what speed the shake starts and what changed before it, offers Friday at 7:30, books it on the number and repeats the time, the work and the number.

facts.note: No price is asked for. The account is on the company-account rate (catalogue.json company_account_terms).

script.said: Thanks for calling Brennan Auto Care, this is Maya. How can I help you?
Maya, Lonnie at Nickajack.
Hey, Lonnie! What've you got for me?
Number eight. It's — it's due for its service, and the driver says the steerin' wheel shakes on the interstate.
Okay. Before I pull it up — have you got a P-O for this one? Donna'll have my head if I open another ticket without it.
I heard about that. Yeah, hang on... It's — it's N-D, six-oh-four-one-eight.
N-D, six-oh-four-one-eight. Got it, it's on there. Okay, number eight — that's the twenty-one Transit, tag ending six-one-two-five?
Yep.
Okay. And the shake — what speed does it start?
He says about sixty. Smooths out some past seventy.
Okay. Did it start after anything? Like new tires, or he hit something?
We put two fronts on it about a month ago. Not y'all — the tire place.
Okay, that helps. That's — that's probably a balance, then. We'll check it when it's in for the service.
That's what I figured.
So I can take it Friday morning at seven-thirty. Would that work?
Friday. Yeah, I can make Friday work.
Okay. I've got number eight down for Friday at seven-thirty on P-O six-oh-four-one-eight, and I'll write it up myself.
Okay.
How long?
The service is about an hour and a half. If it — if it needs the fronts balanced, add maybe thirty minutes. I'll call you before we do anything past that.
Okay.
Good deal.
So that's number eight, Friday at seven-thirty, the P-M service, and we're checking that shake at sixty. All on P-O six-oh-four-one-eight.
You got it.
Thanks, Lonnie! See you Friday.
